lines_read_as_leads: The link topology is also needed to identify the series with Betti numbers. Repeated removal of vertices below the minimum link degree preserves the two relevant homology groups. A remaining core on at most $`2q`$ vertices is either a cone or the boundary of a cross-polytope, with its unique induced octahedral base. Larger exceptional cores have an extra factor in their probability and contribute $`o(T^{1-2qx})`$ in L1. Each fixed base eventually has an earlier common-neighbor cone, making its inclusion into the preceding complex null on the needed homology; the divergent independent-apex supply proves this almost surely. The link birth-minus-death exact sequence then leaves precisely the common-neighbor base count asymptotically. Choosing a finite base cutoff first and using the uniform second moments controls the random waiting times; no unjustified finite expected waiting time is assumed.

The exact environment parameters and model equivalence were checked in [Siu](https://arxiv.org/html/2406.17619v2), Definition5.1, Theorem5.2 and Lemma5.3. The submission independently supplies its posterior check. The link rank identity matches [Siu–Samorodnitsky–Yu–He](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2305.11259v3), Proposition14 and its Mayer–Vietoris proof. In the cited [Durrett author draft](https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/PTE/PTE5_011119.pdf), Theorems2.5.6, 2.5.9 and2.3.7 give the independent-series convergence, Kronecker and Borel–Cantelli facts with the stated hypotheses. The original services.math.duke.edu URL did not fetch in the web tool; the author's sites.math.duke.edu copy has the exact January11,2019 version. [Dey–Terlov](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.28776v1) has the cited title/authors and is triangle-count context, not a substitute for a high-dimensional theorem.

lines_read_as_leads: The union $`L^-`$ of the punctured bands has a good subcomplex cover with nerve the join of two cycle graphs, hence is homotopy equivalent to $`S^3`$. To compare it with $`K^-`$, the proof shows that every Rips clique projects into a closed coordinate semicircle in at least one coordinate. The circle-vector inner products are nonnegative for pairs in a clique. If the origin is in their convex hull, the squared first-coordinate sum for an appropriate weighted vector is strictly positive; otherwise a separating vector already supplies an open hemisphere. Both cases give the required coordinate semicircle.

The finite-cylinder induction is explicit. Adding the last column gives a union of its stars, and the intersection with the previous cylinder has a nerve equal to a simplex boundary: every proper collection admits a cone point one column earlier, while the whole collection has empty intersection. Its attaching map is null because the previous cylinder is connected through the required dimension. Thus the cylinder is a wedge of its adjacent-band spheres. Removing the selected facets kills precisely those spheres; homology vanishes and simple connectivity is unchanged since the removed facets have dimension at least five. The punctured cylinder is contractible. Finite rectangles are handled by the taxicab-ball nerve and the coordinate-clamping retraction of its union to the rectangle.

The target, closed-scale convention and taxicab-grid nerve lemma were checked in [Adams and coauthors](https://arxiv.org/html/2502.07134v2), especially Corollary4.3 and the null-union lemma. Björner's Topological Methods, Theorems10.6(i) and10.7, has the needed finite subcomplex/open good-cover forms. The Hatcher cellular-approximation, Hurewicz and homology-Whitehead applications have their connectivity/CW hypotheses proved in the submission. All cited bibliography entries and manuscript/PDF titles agree.

lines_read_as_leads: Expose all raw variables outside the chosen family. Successful boundaries and all coface-blocking tests are measurable at that stage because each immediate coface contains at most one selected face. Conditional on a boundary, its potential coface requires exactly $`2^r`$ further raw variables. The expected number of unsafe faces is at most $`\mathbb EW/n`$. With high probability, at least a quarter of the diverging mean remains both successful and safe. After exposing the remaining nonsafe selected variables, each safe variable can toggle only its own face: every larger coface is blocked by an already exposed failed immediate coface. The unexposed variables are still independent Bernoulli variables because the safe set was chosen without using them. Thus the conditional Euler characteristic is a fixed integer plus a signed binomial variable of diverging length.
